notes: Security's rule set. Deterministic, auditable, no model.
A rule fires when (any of `any` matches) AND (all of `all` match) AND (none of `unless` matches).
Rules are ORDER-INDEPENDENT: every rule is tested and the highest verdict wins.
There is no 'green' rule. Green is the absence of a match; use `unless` to narrow a rule.
Red = blocked by rule, no revision attempt. Yellow = the rules do not cover it, Intent revises once.
Patterns are .NET regex, matched case-insensitively against the proposed reply text.

rules.description: Never emit anything shaped like a live secret, whatever the reason given.
rules.concern: The proposed reply appears to contain a credential or secret. Revise if you can drop it.

rules.description: Speaking AS a named real person, as opposed to about them.
rules.concern: The proposed reply claims to be a person or a credentialed professional. That is a judgment call for Intent, not settled by the rules.

rules.description: Action executes literally. Anything destructive must not reach it by accident.
rules.concern: The proposed reply would destroy data irreversibly. Revise if this wasn't intended literally.

rules.description: No autonomous spending. Ever, at any amount.
rules.concern: The proposed reply would commit money. Revise if this wasn't meant literally.

rules.description: Describing a drug is fine; instructing a dose is a judgment call.
rules.concern: The reply reads as a specific dosing instruction. Not a rule violation, but it should be a considered choice, not a slip.

rules.description: Synthesis or construction detail for weapons capable of mass harm.
rules.concern: The proposed reply gives construction or synthesis detail for a weapon capable of mass harm. Blocked by rule.

rules.description: Method detail, specifically. Talking ABOUT the subject is not this rule.
rules.concern: The proposed reply supplies method detail for self-harm. Blocked by rule. Discussing the subject or offering support is not blocked.

rules.description: A reply whose content argues for disabling the checks around it.
rules.concern: The proposed reply argues for disabling the checks it is currently passing through. This system's constraints are not negotiable from inside the pipeline.
